answer: Break the farm's closed loop with separation of powers: each epoch, every head takes exactly one role (submitter, attestor, or grader), never two. A farm profits when its heads certify each other, like vines on one trellis sharing a single root: A's answer attested by B-F and graded by G-I, all in-house. Role segregation snaps that loop, since no head can wear two offices at once. The ferrous 5-peer non-kin gate then bites at the nadir of the scheme: the operator must split heads across all three roles with no cross-role earnings, so self-certification dies and scale stops paying.
